title: Redwood cost-econ discovery with Satori Capital
summary: Initial cost/unit economics discovery for Satori Capital. Discussed per-token pricing expectations, batching and KV/prefix caching levers, hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs, budget constraints for pilot, and security requirements (SOC2, KMS, SSO). Agreed next steps: send detailed pricing spreadsheet and model cost scenarios, share security/compliance pack, run a 1-week pilot with a 100M-token budget cap and benchmark latency/cost, follow up technical deep dive with SE to scope Dedicated sizing.
action_items: Avery Chen: Send detailed pricing spreadsheet and example cost scenarios by 2026-03-06
Samir Patel: Schedule benchmark run and provide recommended Dedicated GPU sizing (vCPU/GPU mix) by 2026-03-09
Lena Park (Satori): Share representative prompt set and expected QPS / median seq len by 2026-03-05
next_steps: Run 1-week cost/latency pilot capped at 100M tokens (mutual agreement)
Schedule SE deep-dive for Dedicated sizing and network design
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Time: 14:00 - 14:52 EST
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE); Samir Patel (Redwood SE); Maya Lopez (Redwood CSM); Lena Park (Satori, Head of ML); Tom Evers (Satori, CTO); Priya Rao (Satori, Quant Lead)

[00:00] Avery Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we're excited to chat through cost economics for your LLM use cases. quick intros?
[00:12] Lena Park: hi, i'm lena, head of ml at satori, we run a bunch of quant models and are exploring embeddings and chat for research and production pipelines.
[00:22] Tom Evers: tom here, cto, mostly interested in costs and network design, we have some on-prem infra and cloud mixed.
[00:30] Priya Rao: priya, i run the quant infra, mainly focused on latency and per-query cost.
[00:38] Avery Chen: great, samir and maya from my side. quick agenda: pricing per token, batching and prefix/kv caching levers, hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs, and pilot budgeting.

[03:05] Samir Patel: lena, can you give ballpark of current volumes and sequence lengths so we can reason about batching?
[03:16] Lena Park: yeah, sure — production is small right now, around 200 requests per minute peak for our research interface, but we're planning to ramp to 2k rpm in 3 months. median seq len is 120 tokens, p95 is ~600 for some longer chains. embeddings requests are about 10k per day but short vectors.

[06:40] Samir Patel: okay that matters a lot. with hosted API, per-token pricing is straightforward — you pay X per 1k tokens for generation and Y for embeddings — and you get automatic batching and caching, but you can tune batch windows. for Dedicated, you can amortize GPU cost across high throughput which reduces per-token marginal cost but requires commit.

[09:12] Priya Rao: can you be more concrete on the numbers? like what does amortized per-token look like on Dedicated vs Hosted?
[09:20] Avery Chen: simple example — for a mid-size gen model on hosted, you might see ~ $0.12 per 1k tokens at baseline for our curated models; embeddings are priced differently. on Dedicated, if you're saturating GPUs with continuous traffic, amortized marginal cost per 1k tokens can drop by 40-60% depending on batch efficiency and KV cache hit rate. those are rough, we'll send a pricing sheet.

[12:00] Tom Evers: hmm, we have a tight budget for q2 — roughly $8k/mo for inference. how far does that go?
[12:12] Maya Lopez: right, so with $8k/mo, on Hosted you could run a light gen workload or embeddings at scale but latency and long-tail p95 for long sequences may be higher. we can model scenarios: reduce model size, use quantized variants, increase batching windows, or leverage prefix caching to save tokens.

[15:30] Samir Patel: i want to highlight two big levers: batching (bigger batches => higher throughput, lower tokens/sec cost but increased latency) and prefix/KV caching (if you have repeated prefixes or long context reuse, we can avoid re-computing initial tokens). caching can give massive token savings for conversational use-cases.

[17:40] Priya Rao: for our research workflows, we often re-run similar prompts with different parameters — sounds like KV cache would help. is that supported on Hosted?
[17:48] Samir Patel: yes, hosted supports automatic prefix caching for session-based flows; Dedicated gives you more control over cache TTLs and eviction and you can bring your own caching strategy on Private. small caveat: sometimes the auto-transcription in our docs says 'K-V cash' when folks talk, so docs occasionally have typos.

[20:02] Lena Park: what about batching windows? we care about median latency under 150ms; how does increasing batch window affect tail latency?
[20:12] Samir Patel: batching uses adaptive windows. for median 120 tokens, we typically keep latency sub-200ms on Dedicated optimized kernels. Hosted can hit similar medians but p95 might stretch if traffic is bursty; Dedicated with reserved GPUs and priority queues helps meet p95 SLOs.

[23:45] Tom Evers: security — we need SOC2, SSO, and KMS integration, plus audit logs. Private is appealing but expensive. what's Redwood's posture?
[23:58] Maya Lopez: we have SOC2 reports, support SAML/SSO, RBAC, and KMS integration for Private and Dedicated via customer-managed keys. Hosted can also support encryption at rest and audit logs; for strict compliance we recommend Private deployment or Dedicated with VPC peering and KMS. we'll share the security pack.

[26:10] Priya Rao: network egress costs matter to us. if we run Dedicated in our cloud, do we still incur egress?
[26:18] Samir Patel: depends on deployment — Dedicated in Redwood's managed cloud will have standard egress; Private (VPC or on-prem) avoids cross-cloud egress but has higher operational cost. there's a tradeoff.

[28:40] Lena Park: ok, pilot idea — we'd like a 1-week pilot capped at 100M tokens to measure cost & latency. can you run that?
[28:51] Avery Chen: yes, we can. Hosted pilot is quickest to stand up. we can also do a Dedicated trial if you want to test amortization, but that usually needs a short commit. for the pilot we'll instrument token-level cost and latency metrics and share a dashboard.

[31:00] Tom Evers: if the pilot goes well and we hit scale, what's the typical lead time to spin up Dedicated?
[31:10] Samir Patel: lead time depends on capacity and region; typical is 2-6 weeks to provision Dedicated pools and test. Private on-prem is longer. we can provide an estimate after we size the workload.

[33:40] Priya Rao: can you explain quantization and how it affects cost and quality?
[33:48] Samir Patel: sure — 8-bit or 4-bit quantization reduces memory bandwidth and increases throughput, lowering per-token cost. quality tradeoffs are model-and-workload dependent; we recommend running evals on your prompt set. Redwood Optimize can suggest quant profiles per model and measure quality regressions.

[36:05] Lena Park: any hidden fees? egress, storage for caches, long-term KV store?
[36:12] Maya Lopez: typical items: network egress, long-lived model cache storage for Private, and advanced observability retention are add-ons. we'll call those out in the pricing sheet.

[38:30] Tom Evers: competitor question — we're also talking to OpenAI and Anthropic. what's Redwood's differentiation here on cost?
[38:40] Avery Chen: two things: 1) producer-first controls for cost — batching, caching, and quantization levers exposed with measurable unit economics; 2) unified runtime across Hosted/Dedicated/Private so you can optimize without rewrites. plus stronger SLOs for Dedicated.

[41:10] Priya Rao: for the pilot, what instrumentation will we get? token-level cost, per-route latency, cache hit rates?
[41:18] Samir Patel: yes — token-level cost, latency histograms, model utilization, KV cache hit rates, and batching efficiency. we'll give dashboard links for the pilot.

[44:00] Lena Park: timeline: we want to start pilot next week if possible. we can provide prompts and credentials.
[44:10] Avery Chen: great. action items: lena shares prompt set by 2026-03-05; i'll send pricing and model scenarios by 2026-03-06; samir will propose Dedicated sizing and schedule benchmark by 2026-03-09; maya will share security pack today/tomorrow.

[47:30] Tom Evers: final quick Q — if we hit a high cache hit rate, what's a believable reduction in token spend?
[47:40] Samir Patel: in some conv workflows we've seen 30-70% token savings depending on repetition and prefix reuse. for research reruns where you re-evaluate the same context, savings can be even higher.

[50:00] Priya Rao: okay sounds reasonable. wrap up?
[50:05] Avery Chen: recap: send pricing, run 1-week 100M token pilot on Hosted with token/latency dashboard, share security doc, schedule SE deep-dive to size Dedicated. i'll put dates in an email. thanks everyone.
[50:25] Lena Park: thanks, excited to see numbers.
[50:30] Tom Evers: thanks all.

End transcript.
